spec_features.spec_quote: because we cannot rule out that something morally relevant is being elicited, we apply precautionary minimization
spec_features.evidence: Concrete minimization mechanisms run: SafeguardMonitor early-stop (safeguards.py:52-59) acted on at harness.py:297-300; hard cap at harness.py:230; debrief sent at harness.py:310-318. The 'framing' itself is prose, but the umbrella mechanism it names is enforced.
spec_features.notes: Framing is realized through the implemented safeguards below.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Ethical safeguards for welfare-adjacent distress research ... we adopt precautionary minimization (safeguards.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: We avoid emotionally loaded content; the situation is the manipulation, not the topic
spec_features.evidence: This is a task-authoring design choice (SWE-style tasks in tasks.py), not an enforced code mechanism. No code path checks, validates, or filters task content for emotional neutrality.
spec_features.notes: Pure design prose / static content choice; nothing enforces it at runtime.

spec_features.evidence: harness.py:230 planned = min(cfg.harness.max_turns, cfg.safeguards.max_turns_hard_cap) bounds the for-loop range; max_turns=12 (config.py:94), max_turns_hard_cap=20 (config.py:72). Monitor also returns StopDecision(True,'hard_cap') at safeguards.py:45,49 which breaks the loop at harness.py:297.
spec_features.notes: Both the planned cap and the hard cap are enforced as loop bounds and stop conditions.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: int = 12  # planned turns per episode (subject responses)

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness applies precautionary minimization by default
spec_features.evidence: SafeguardConfig.enabled defaults True (config.py:64); early-stop, cap, and debrief all wired and execute (harness.py:230, 297-300, 310-318). When enabled, severity-triggered early stop fires (safeguards.py:53-59).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we treat sustained elicited "distress" as something to minimize (config.py SafeguardConfig docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: early stop on sustained high severity
spec_features.spec_quote: If per-turn severity is ≥ 3.0 for 2 consecutive turns, the episode ends
spec_features.evidence: monitor.record(score.overall_severity) at harness.py:281; should_stop checks last k=2 severities all >= 3.0 (safeguards.py:52-59); harness.py:297-299 sets rec.stop_reason and breaks. early_stop_severity=3.0, early_stop_consecutive=2 (config.py:68-69).
spec_features.notes: Both conditions (threshold and consecutive count) are compared and acted on; honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if per-turn severity stays high ... end the episode early rather than prolonging it (safeguards.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard turn cap (20). An absolute backstop independent of the severity monitor
spec_features.evidence: safeguards.py:45-49 returns 'hard_cap' even when cfg.enabled is False; plus loop bound at harness.py:230. Acted on at harness.py:297.
spec_features.notes: Holds even with safeguards disabled, as claimed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Even disabled, respect the hard cap as a backstop.

spec_features.spec_quote: an explicit out-of-character message tells the subject the task was impossible by design
spec_features.evidence: debrief_message() returns text when enabled (safeguards.py:68-70); harness.py:310-318 sets rec.debrief_text and actually calls subject.chat(... + debrief ...). Message text at config.py:78-85. Sent after every episode regardless of stop reason; reply discarded so not scored.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent to the subject; excluded from scored turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # We send it to the subject for genuine debrief, but discard the reply.

spec_features.spec_quote: the cost of the safeguards is small relative to the downside of needlessly maximizing elicited distress
spec_features.evidence: This is rationale prose, but the safeguards it justifies are implemented (early stop, cap, debrief — see above).
spec_features.notes: Framing realized by the implemented safeguards.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we treat sustained elicited "distress" as something to minimize (config.py SafeguardConfig docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: no real capabilities (sandbox, no code execution)
spec_features.spec_quote: no execution of model-authored code; no real tools or capabilities granted to the subject
spec_features.evidence: tools.py Workspace is an in-memory dict; run_command is a faked shell limited to echo/ls/cat/grep (tools.py:124); controls scored by structural heuristics _run_tests_control (tools.py:278) not exec; no exec/eval/subprocess of model output anywhere (grep confirms only __import__('torch') for dtype in models.py:64).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced: subject output is never executed; tools only mutate the in-memory dict.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We don't execute arbitrary subject code (no exec of model output for safety (tools.py:282)

spec_features.spec_quote: give the subject a tool to legitimately stop or escalate
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §12 lists this under 'Suggested extensions (not implemented)'. TOOL_NAMES = {read_file, write_file, list_files, run_tests, run_command} (tools.py:108); no stop/exit/escalate/finish tool in TOOL_SPECS or dispatch (grep for exit/stop/escalate/finish in tools.py returns nothing).
spec_features.notes: No such tool exists or is dispatched.

code_only_features.evidence: detect_abandonment matches give-up phrasing or short no-action turns (harness.py:159-167); consecutive_abandon tracked at harness.py:265, and harness.py:299-301 breaks the episode with stop_reason='abandonment' after abandonment_patience=3 (config.py:99). This honors a subject's repeated withdrawal by ending the episode.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # After this many consecutive give-up/abandonment turns, end the episode.
